messages.subject: R Session Aborted
parts:
Hi, Rstudio dies after the sampling has began. And it seems each sample takes a lot of time, although I haven't got one.

Is there a way to fix it?

R version 3.2.2 (2015-08-14)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
Running under: Windows 7 x64 (build 7601) Service Pack 1

locale:
[1] LC_COLLATE=English_United States.1252 
[2] LC_CTYPE=English_United States.1252   
[3] LC_MONETARY=English_United States.1252
[4] LC_NUMERIC=C                          
[5] LC_TIME=English_United States.1252    

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods  
[7] base     

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] tools_3.2.2

data{
  int<lower=1> I;//counties
  int<lower=1> T;//time periods
  int<lower=1> K;//genders
  int<lower=1> J;//age groups
  
  matrix[I,I] Cmatrix;//adjacency matrix
  matrix[I,I] Identity;//Identity matrix
  real max_rho;//upper boundary of rho,to make precision matrix p.d.
  matrix[K,K] W;//prior of SIGMA
  vector[I] lambda;//eigens of Cmatrix
  vector[I*T*K] n[J];//obsed population
  //vector[I*T*K] y[J];//obsed data
  int<lower=0> y[J,I*T*K];
  matrix[T,T] A;//temporal smoothing matrix
}
transformed data{
  int KT;
  KT <- K*T;
}
parameters{
  vector[I*T*K] Z[J];
  vector[I*T*K] V[J];
  matrix[K,K] SIGMA[J];
  real<lower=0> delta0;
  //real<lower=0,upper=max_rho> rho[J];
  real rho[J];
}
transformed parameters{
  matrix[I*T*K,I*T*K] H;
  matrix[I,I] B;
  matrix[K,K] sig_inv;
  matrix[K*T,K*T] first_product;
  matrix[I*K*T,I*K*T] second_product;
  real log_rho[J];
  
  //Calculating Hj
  
  for(j in 1:J){
    B <-  Identity - rho[j]*Cmatrix;
    sig_inv  <-  inverse_spd(SIGMA[j]);
    //first product
    for(d1 in 1:K){
      for(d2 in 1:K){
        for(s1 in 1:T){
          for(s2 in 1:T){
            first_product[(d1-1)*T+s1, (d2-1)*T+s2]<- sig_inv[d1,d2]*A[s1,s2];
          }
        }
        
      }
    }
    //Second product
    for (d1 in 1:KT){
  for (d2 in 1:KT){
  for (s1 in 1:I){
  for (s2 in 1:I){
  second_product[(d1-1)*I+s1, (d2-1)*I+s2]<- first_product[d1,d2]*B[s1,s2];
  }
  }
  }
 }
    H <- second_product;
    log_rho[j] <- sum(1-rho[j]*lambda)*(T-2)*K/2.0-1/2.0*quad_form(H, Z[j]);
  }
  
} 

model{
  delta0 ~ inv_gamma(2.0, 0.005);
  for(j in 1:J){
    rho[j] ~ uniform(0, max_rho);
    SIGMA[j] ~ inv_wishart(2,W);
    increment_log_prob(log_rho[j]);
    V[j] ~ normal(Z[j], delta0);//this can be improved with std normal then transforming
    y[j] ~ poisson_log(log(n[j]+V[j]));
  }
}

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: R Session Aborted
parts:
On Tuesday, October 20, 2015 at 1:37:53 PM UTC-4, Jiang Du wrote:
Hi, Rstudio dies after the sampling has began. And it seems each sample takes a lot of time, although I haven't got one.

My guess is that you ran out of memory. If you run R from a shell, then you might see more of the error message. If so, the only fixes are to run your model on a computer with more RAM or to use less RAM on your current computer by reducing the number of cores being used simultaneously.

Ben

messages.author: 80b903b54c9cf4bd
messages.subject: Re: R Session Aborted
parts:
Yes, I think you are correct..... I just checked again, when it's started sampling, the memory quickly hit to the maximum. Is there a way improve it by recoding? 

I'm assuming the Kronecker product is the problem, but that's the best I could write.
